extracted.intended_audience: aspiring writers seeking to submit manuscripts to HarperCollins
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting a book manuscript to HarperCollins: formatting, cover letter and synopsis, selecting the correct imprint, understanding rights/contracts, and preparing for editorial revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission Format and Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting your manuscript, ensure it aligns with the basic formatting requirements. HarperCollins typically expects manuscripts to be double-spaced with a readable font like Times New Roman or Arial in 12-point size. Margins should be one inch on all sides, and the text should be left-aligned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard format ensures that your manuscript is easy to read and professionally presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover Letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a cover letter that succinctly introduces yourself and your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This letter should capture the essence of your manuscript and its market potential. Remember, first impressions are crucial!

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeting the Right Imprint
rubrics_metrics.description: HarperCollins operates several imprints, each catering to different genres and audiences. It's vital to research and identify the imprint that best fits your manuscript (e.g., HarperTeen for young adult, Avon for romance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each imprint may have specific submission guidelines, so ensure you tailor your submission accordingly. This specificity demonstrates your understanding of the publisher's needs and increases the likelihood of a positive response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding Copyright and Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting to HarperCollins, it's essential to understand the rights you are granting. Typically, the publisher will seek exclusive rights to publish your work in specific formats and regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always read the contract carefully and consider consulting a literary agent or attorney if you have questions about your rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crafting a Compelling Synopsis
rubrics_metrics.description: A well-crafted synopsis should provide a clear overview of your story, including key plot points and character arcs, while being concise and engaging. Aim for one to two pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The synopsis should highlight what makes your story unique and why it will appeal to readers. Treat it as an opportunity to sell your story—be concise, compelling, and focused on market potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing for Possible Revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if your manuscript is accepted, expect to go through several rounds of revisions. HarperCollins editors work closely with authors to refine and enhance the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be open to feedback and willing to make changes as needed. Embrace revisions as a collaborative opportunity for growth that leads to a polished final product.
